questions.question: Spanreeds are the most widespread use of which kind of fabrial?
choices: Augmenters
Conjoiners made from a split ruby
Reversers made from amethyst
Warning fabrials
questions.explanation: Conjoiners, a type of pairing fabrial, are made from a split ruby and move in parallel over great distances. Spanreeds are their most common use.

questions.question: What is a dead Shardblade?
choices: A broken Honorblade
A deadeye spren whose Radiant broke their oaths
A Shardblade with no gemstone in its hilt
A Blade that can no longer be summoned
questions.explanation: Dead Shardblades are deadeye spren that perished when their Radiant broke their oaths. They can't change shape, but can still form a rudimentary bond and be summoned.

questions.question: Towerlight is a hybrid of which two Lights?
choices: Stormlight and Voidlight
Stormlight and Lifelight
Lifelight and Voidlight
Stormlight and anti-Stormlight
questions.explanation: Towerlight (the Sibling's essence) combines Stormlight and Lifelight. Warlight, discovered by Navani and Raboniel, combines Stormlight and Voidlight.

questions.question: What is raysium?
choices: A soft metal used for fabrial frames
A God Metal from Odium that siphons Stormlight
A type of perfect gemstone
The alloy that Shardplate is forged from
questions.explanation: Raysium is a God Metal from the Shard Odium. The Fused make weapons from it that siphon Stormlight, and set with anti-Light gems they can kill Invested beings.

questions.question: What natural rock formations protect Kholinar from highstorms?
choices: The Misted Mountains
Windblades
Laits
Chasms
questions.explanation: Kholinar, Alethkar's symmetrical capital from the Silver Kingdoms era, is built around large rock formations called windblades.

questions.question: Which revived Alethi title has authority over criminal investigations, policing and appointing judges?
choices: Highprince of War
Highprince of Commerce
Highprince of Information
Highprince of Works
questions.explanation: The Highprince of Information oversees investigations, policing and judicial appointments. Commerce covers merchants and roads, War covers military matters, and Works covers infrastructure, including Stormlight management.

questions.question: In the Vorin caste system, who holds the first dahn?
choices: The highprinces
The monarch alone
Shardbearers
The ardents
questions.explanation: Lighteyes are ranked in dahns (first highest). The first dahn belongs solely to the monarch, the second to the highprinces. Darkeyes are ranked in nahns, and the tenth nahn can be sold into slavery.

questions.question: In Vorin Alethkar, who are the only people permitted to use Soulcasters?
choices: Highprinces
Ardents
Stormwardens
Shardbearers
questions.explanation: Ardents — Vorin priests who can't own property or hold political office — are the only ones allowed to use Soulcasters, which gives them great influence.

questions.question: The Thrill, the battle rage concentrated in Alethkar, was caused by which Unmade?
choices: Moelach
Sja-anat
Nergaoul
Ba-Ado-Mishram
questions.explanation: The Thrill came from the Unmade Nergaoul, whose influence was concentrated in Alethkar during the Era of Solitude.

questions.question: How much real power does the Prime Aqasix of Azir hold?
choices: Absolute power over the whole empire
A figurehead whom the viziers can overrule
Command of the military, and nothing else
None; the office is purely hereditary
questions.explanation: The viziers elect the Prime Aqasix, who is a revered figurehead with limited power. Viziers guide the Prime and can even overrule them.

questions.question: Why do Tashikki people wear shiquas, full-body wraps?
choices: To protect themselves from highstorm debris
To hide from Nun Raylisi's hateful gaze
To show their rank in the bureaucracy
As a sign of mourning for the Heralds
questions.explanation: Tashikki worship Tashi (the Herald Ishar) and believe in an evil god, Nun Raylisi (based on Odium). Shiquas shield the wearer from his hateful gaze.

questions.question: Who is Tezim, the veiled god-priest of Tukar, secretly?
choices: The Herald Nale
The Herald Ishar
Taravangian
A Fused
questions.explanation: Unknown to the Tukari, their god-priest Tezim is the Herald Ishar.

questions.question: What is unusual about Herdazian fingernails?
choices: They glow faintly in total darkness
They're crystalline and spark like flint
They grow into hard carapace plates
They're naturally a deep blue color
questions.explanation: Thanks to distant singer ancestry, Herdazian nails are crystalline and spark like flint against steel. Herdazians use them with 'sparkflickers' to start fires.

cite.section: Ch. 2 Nations and Cultures › Herdazian Culture

questions.question: In an Unkalaki family, which son is tasked with becoming a warrior?
choices: The first son
The second son
The third son
The fourth son
questions.explanation: First and second sons farm, raise livestock or hunt; third sons become craftsmen; fourth sons become warriors. Younger brothers shift up if an older son can't serve.

cite.section: Ch. 2 Nations and Cultures › Horneater Peaks (Family Structure)

questions.question: Where is the only stable entry point to Roshar for offworld visitors?
choices: The Origin of Storms, far to the east
Cultivation's Perpendicularity in the Pool
The Oathgate in Thaylen City
Honor's Perpendicularity at Urithiru
questions.explanation: Cultivation's Perpendicularity lies in the Unkalaki crater lake called the Pool. It's the only stable entry for worldhoppers, whom the Unkalaki greet as 'strange gods.'

cite.section: Ch. 2 Nations and Cultures › Offworld Visitors

questions.question: According to the Iriali Long Trail, what is Roshar?
choices: The final world, where the One reunites
The fourth of seven worlds on their journey
Their original homeworld
A prison world
questions.explanation: The Iriali believe Roshar is the fourth world on a seven-world journey, after which they'll reunite as the One. Many keep packs ready to leave at a moment's notice.

questions.question: Of the nations that enslaved singers, which is the only one where humans and singers achieved peace after the Everstorm?
choices: Azir
Thaylenah
Iri
Jah Keved
questions.explanation: Iriali humans acknowledged the singers as the land's rightful stewards and began a peaceful surrender, complicated later by the Fused taking control of Iri's military.

cite.section: Ch. 2 Nations and Cultures › Iriali and Riran Singers

questions.question: How are Kharbranth's free public hospitals funded?
choices: Taxes on spanreed traffic
Revenue from the Palanaeum
Donations from the Vorin church
Sale of Soulcast grain
questions.explanation: Treatment is free because the hospitals are fully funded by revenue from the Palanaeum, Roshar's largest library, which charges expensive admission.

cite.section: Ch. 2 Nations and Cultures › Kharbranth (Medical Prowess)

questions.question: How do the Selay of the Purelake handle their two brother gods?
choices: They worship both brothers equally
Honor Vun Makak openly; worship Nu Ralik in secret
They reject both gods entirely
Worship Vun Makak openly and fear Nu Ralik
questions.explanation: Their true god is the upright Nu Ralik, but to avoid his jealous brother's ire they pretend to venerate Vun Makak, saving worship of Nu Ralik for holy grottos.

cite.section: Ch. 2 Nations and Cultures › Selay Culture (Religion)

questions.question: Where do warriors rank in Shin society?
choices: At the top, as honored protectors
At the bottom, as 'those who subtract'
Equal to farmers, as 'those who add'
Just below the Honorbearers
questions.explanation: The Shin divide people into 'those who add' (farmers are highly respected) and 'those who subtract.' Anyone who takes up a weapon is forever a lowly warrior in brown, subject to the Stone Shamans.

cite.section: Ch. 2 Nations and Cultures › Shinovar (Social Ranking)

questions.question: What is a 'babsk' in Thaylen merchant culture?
choices: A captain's twenty-foot ownership rope
A master merchant who is an apprentice's legal parent
A tax paid to the merchant guilds
A note drawn on the Thaylen Gemstone Reserve
questions.explanation: Would-be merchants apprentice to a master merchant who becomes their babsk — their legal parent — until declaring them ready to strike out on their own.

cite.section: Ch. 2 Nations and Cultures › Thaylenah (Resources and Trade)

questions.question: Which spren must a singer bond during a highstorm to take warform?
choices: Windspren
Gravitationspren
Painspren
Lifespren
questions.explanation: Warform comes from bonding a painspren. Nimbleform uses windspren, workform gravitationspren, and mateform lifespren.

cite.section: Ch. 2 Nations and Cultures › Recovered Forms

questions.question: Why did the listeners retain their free will when other singers lost theirs?
choices: They lived beyond the Everstorm's reach
They had refused Ba-Ado-Mishram's Connection
They had bonded honorspren as protectors
The Heralds personally shielded them
questions.explanation: The listeners rejected Ba-Ado-Mishram's offer and Connection. When the Radiants imprisoned her, every singer Connected to her was severed — but not the listeners, who were left with only dullform and mateform.

cite.section: Ch. 2 Nations and Cultures › The Listeners

questions.question: What notable ability does the Regal envoyform grant?
choices: Channeling red lightning to strike at foes
Understanding any language after a few sentences
Flight through the open air on Voidlight
Heavy, armor-like carapace over the whole body
questions.explanation: Envoyform Regals can speak, read and understand any human or singer language after hearing just a few sentences. Stormform is the one that channels red lightning.

cite.section: Ch. 2 Nations and Cultures › Regal Forms

questions.question: Into how many Shards was Adonalsium split at the Shattering?
choices: Three
Ten
Sixteen
Twenty
questions.explanation: Conspirators used the Dawnshards to kill Adonalsium, fracturing the power of creation into sixteen Shards, each with its own Intent.

cite.section: Ch. 3 Cosmology and Religion › Shattering of Adonalsium

questions.question: Which of these Shards was NOT killed by Odium?
choices: Honor
Devotion
Cultivation
Ambition
questions.explanation: Odium killed Ambition, Devotion, Dominion and Honor. Cultivation survives and remains on Roshar.

cite.section: Ch. 3 Cosmology and Religion › Dead Shards

questions.question: What is Braize?
choices: Roshar's largest and brightest moon, Nomon
A cold planet where the Fused's souls are bound
The ancient capital city of Shinovar
The singers' traditional name for Shadesmar
questions.explanation: Braize, the third terrestrial planet of the Rosharan system, has a metal core that draws in Investiture. The Fused's souls are bound there, migrating to Roshar during Desolations.

cite.section: Ch. 3 Cosmology and Religion › Terrestrial Planets

questions.question: Which of Roshar's moons always rises first each night, and what color is it?
choices: Nomon, pale blue
Mishim, green
Salas, violet
Salas, red
questions.explanation: Salas (violet, associated with Odium) rises first, then Nomon (pale blue, Honor), then Mishim (green, Cultivation). Only during the 17th hour, the 'hateful hour,' is no moon visible.

questions.question: Who is the Vessel of Cultivation?
choices: Tanavast, a human tanner
Rayse, a Shin man
Koravellium Avast, a dragon
The Nightwatcher
questions.explanation: Koravellium Avast (Koravari), a dragon who often takes human form, holds Cultivation. She loved Tanavast, the Vessel of Honor, until he betrayed Ba-Ado-Mishram.

questions.question: Under the contract Tanavast forged with Honor's power, how can Odium claim Roshar?
choices: By outlasting the Heralds on Braize
Only through a contest of champions
By capturing and holding Urithiru
By ending the highstorms for good
questions.explanation: Even after Honor's Vessel fell, Odium stayed bound by the contract: he can only claim Roshar through a contest of champions.

cite.section: Ch. 3 Cosmology and Religion › Odium (Power and Works)

questions.question: Which Herald, patron of the Stonewards, was the only one who never broke under torture?
choices: Jezrien
Kalak
Talenel
Ishar
questions.explanation: Talenel (Taln), Herald of War and patron of the Stonewards, never broke, even when the other nine abandoned the Oathpact and left him to bear it alone.

questions.question: When Vorin characters swear 'Kelek's breath!', which Herald are they invoking?
choices: Kalak
Chanaranach
Jezrien
Battar
questions.explanation: Kalak is known as Kelek in Vorinism because of a vowel shift. He's patron of the Willshapers and a very common expletive.

questions.question: How was Ba-Ado-Mishram defeated at the end of the False Desolation?
choices: She was slain by Talenel with his Honorblade
Melishi bonded her and trapped her in a gemstone
The Heralds banished her to Braize
She surrendered to the Knights Radiant
questions.explanation: Melishi, acting on Tanavast's orders, used a bond with Mishram to pull her into a perfect gemstone. All singers Connected to her lost their forms and Identity.

questions.question: Which Unmade 'Enlightens' (corrupts) spren and secretly works against Odium?
choices: Re-Shephir
Sja-anat
Ashertmarn
Dai-Gonarthis
questions.explanation: Sja-anat, the Taker of Secrets, corrupts spren with Odium's Investiture. She pretends to serve Odium but actively works against him and encourages her 'children' to bond Radiants.

questions.question: The prophetic 'death rattles' of the dying are attributed to which Unmade?
choices: Moelach
Nergaoul
Chemoarish
Yelig-nar
questions.explanation: Moelach's domain is precognition. He's said to possess the minds of the dying, whose last words Kharbranthian scholars secretly study as prophecy.

questions.question: Each brand of Fused accesses a single surge. Which surge can no Fused use?
choices: Gravitation
Adhesion
Transformation
Illumination
questions.explanation: The nine Fused brands cover nine surges (e.g. Heavenly Ones use Gravitation, Deepest Ones use Cohesion), but no Fused can access Adhesion.

cite.section: Ch. 3 Cosmology and Religion › Brands of Fused

questions.question: How does Vorinism view symmetry?
choices: As a sign of Odium's corruption
Holy, though names mustn't be too symmetrical
As irrelevant to faith or daily life
Reserved for the Almighty's name alone
questions.explanation: Symmetry is holy in Vorinism: glyphs and the Heralds' names are symmetrical, and many people's names are nearly so — but making them too symmetrical is impious.

questions.question: According to the true history revealed in the Eila Stele, who were the original 'Voidbringers'?
choices: The Fused
The Unmade
Humans from Ashyn
The thunderclasts
questions.explanation: Humans fled the ruined world of Ashyn to Roshar. Because they brought Odium with them, the Dawnsingers named them the Voidbringers.

cite.section: Ch. 4 History of Roshar › Odium's Influence (False History)

questions.question: Which Radiant order did NOT take part in the Recreance?
choices: The Windrunners
The Skybreakers
The Bondsmiths
The Edgedancers
questions.explanation: After Tanavast's vision, the Radiants and their spren agreed together to break their oaths, killing the spren. Only the Skybreakers abstained, withdrawing to ensure the Radiants never rose again.

questions.question: What does 'Parshendi', the Alethi name for the listeners, mean?
choices: 'Children of the storm'
'Parshmen who can think'
'Those who sing'
'Free people'
questions.explanation: When Gavilar's expedition met the listeners, the Alethi, ignorant of singer history, called them Parshendi — 'parshmen who can think.'

cite.section: Ch. 4 History of Roshar › The Parshendi

questions.question: Who overthrew the Vorin Hierocracy in the War of Loss?
choices: Gavilar Kholin
The Sunmaker
Nohadon
Taravangian
questions.explanation: Sadees, the Sunmaker, united Alethkar's princedoms and cast down the Hierocracy. His empire fractured among his sons after his sudden death.

cite.section: Ch. 4 History of Roshar › War of Loss

questions.question: At the Battle of Thaylen Field, what did Dalinar do to turn the tide?
choices: Slew Odium's champion in single combat
Opened Honor's Perpendicularity
Activated every Oathgate at once
Summoned the Stormfather's highstorm
questions.explanation: Dalinar used his Bondsmith powers to unite the Physical, Cognitive and Spiritual Realms, opening Honor's Perpendicularity. Gems filled with Stormlight and Odium fled.

questions.question: What are the 'seas' of Shadesmar made of?
choices: Black water that can't be swum
Glass beads, each the soul of an object
Thick mist laced with Stormlight
Liquid Investiture from the Spiritual Realm
questions.explanation: Shadesmar's oceans are dark glass beads, each the soul of a non-living object. They drag people down, are drawn to Stormlight, and drift back toward their object's location if moved.

questions.question: How does Shadesmar's geography relate to the Physical Realm?
choices: It's an exact copy of the Physical Realm
Roughly inverted: bead seas mirror its lands
It has no relation to the Physical Realm
It's the same map, rotated 90 degrees
questions.explanation: Shadesmar's seas of beads correspond to Roshar's land and its obsidian lands to the oceans, rivers and lakes. Sizes are shaped by how much people think about an area.

questions.question: What's strange about shadows cast by Shadesmar's small white sun?
choices: Nothing casts shadows there
They point toward the sun
They glow in faint colors
They constantly shift and move
questions.explanation: Shadesmar's sun never moves, and shadows it creates point toward it. Other light sources, like manifested fires, cast normal shadows.

questions.question: In Shadesmar, what do the small floating flames represent?
choices: Lesser spren drawn to emotion
The souls of living creatures
Infused gemstones in the Physical Realm
Fabrials and their captured spren
questions.explanation: Beads are the souls of objects; flames are the souls of living creatures, larger for sapient beings. A flame corrupted by Odium or Sja-anat turns vivid red.

questions.question: What is notable about Lasting Integrity, the honorspren capital?
choices: It floats above the Sea of Souls
Each wall has its own gravity
It's built entirely from manifested beads
It sits atop Cultivation's Perpendicularity
questions.explanation: Lasting Integrity, in the Sea of Souls, is a hollow, roofless blue-stone fortress. Each wall has its own gravitational field, so buildings rise from the walls. The Herald Kalak serves there as High Judge.

questions.question: In Shadesmar, what do luckspren (called mandras there) do for spren sailors?
choices: Navigate by the unmoving sun
Pull their ships through the beads
Light the decks at night
Ward off packs of angerspren
questions.explanation: Mandras are far larger in Shadesmar, with sinuous bodies and arrow-shaped heads. Radiant spren sailors use them to pull ships through the bead sea.

questions.question: For travelers in Shadesmar, what does the World Guide call the greatest dangers?
choices: Packs of angerspren
Dehydration and starvation
Fused warships
Drowning in the bead seas
questions.explanation: Shadesmar's wilderness has no food or water to forage, so supplies are the real threat. Spren traders sell rations, and hydrator fabrials condense water from the air.

cite.section: Ch. 7 Shadesmar › Food, Water, and Survival

questions.question: A non-Radiant PC in Shadesmar wants to manifest a rope from its bead using Stormlight from an unencased gem they're carrying. What's the test?
choices: A DC 15 Insight test
Discipline at the usual DC (often 10) + 5
A DC 10 Crafting test
None — only Radiants can manifest beads
questions.explanation: Manifesting needs a Discipline test (usually DC 10) and 1+ Investiture infused into the bead. Without personal Investiture you can infuse from an unencased gem, but the DC rises by 5. The object then spends 1 Investiture per day.

questions.question: A Windrunner in Shadesmar wants their honorspren to quietly scout ahead (Covert Scouting) and to summon them as a Shardblade. What happens?
choices: Both work normally
Neither works in Shadesmar
Scouting works, but the Blade doesn't
The Blade works, but scouting doesn't
questions.explanation: In Shadesmar, a Radiant spren can't change shape, fly or disappear, so it loses Covert Scouting and Sudden Warning. Radiant and dead Shardblades can't be summoned there; only Honorblades work normally.

questions.question: A PC tests their Gravitation surge while standing near a sea of beads. What special rule applies?
choices: No special rule applies
Raise the stakes on the test
The surge automatically fails
The surge costs double Investiture
questions.explanation: Beads are drawn to Investiture, so surge tests near a bead sea always raise the stakes. The PC can spend an Opportunity to ride the flow 15 ft; the GM can spend a Complication to knock them off their feet (1d6 impact), possibly into the sea.

cite.section: Ch. 7 Shadesmar › Dangers of the Seas

questions.question: A PC with 2 Investiture touches a bead barehanded to learn what it represents. Do they need a test?
choices: Yes — a DC 15 Insight test
No — being Invested is enough
Yes — a DC 10 Discipline test
Only if they're a Radiant
questions.explanation: Touching a bead gives a glimpse of its object if you're currently Invested (1+ Investiture) or succeed on a DC 15 Insight test. Touching too many beads at once is overwhelming.

cite.section: Ch. 7 Shadesmar › Gleaning Impressions From Beads
